newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST- HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST- HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Lo Tak-shing, who was the first person to express the intention to run for the post of chief executive, withdrew from the competition, opening the way for the candidacy of former Appeal Court judge Simon Li.
-- APPLE DAILY -- Chinese dissident Wang Dan was charged by the Beijing government with writing to the Hong Kong and Taiwan press attacking the Communist Party.
-- SING TAO -- About 650,000 people in Hong Kong are suffering from "absolute poverty", meaning they cannot afford basic expenses such as food and shelter. Housing was their biggest problem.

-- Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO -- Beijing stressed the "one country, two systems" principle and said that Hong Kong media had misinterpreted the remarks made by Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen in an interview with the Asian Wall Street Journal.
-- Chinese President Jiang Zemin talked about the Long March, saying it proved that the Communist Party should have absolute control over the army.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Asia Pacific Telecommunications, which has indicated its intention to go public by the end of the year, planned to sign a cooperation deal with a mainland company to explore the mainland satellite broadcasting market in 1999.
-- COMMERCIAL DAILY -- Cotton yarn imports from China decreased by 20 percent in the first seven months of the year, due to increasing raw material costs in China.
-- China will invite tenders for the 1997 textile and garment quotas, to raise export prices and prevent dumping on the European and American markets.

-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Britain will use diplomatic channels to express its alarm at remarks made by Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen on limits to freedom of expression in post-handover Hong Kong.

-- Virgin Atlantic Airways was looking closely at taking a stake in mainland carriers China Eastern or Shanghai Airlines as part of a broader bid to become the first carrier to operate on the London-Shanghai route.

-- Red-chip Silver Grant International Industries and China's most profitable department store operator, Wangfujing, team up to build a chain of up to 50 department stores in a bid to become China's version of Wal-Mart.
-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- The upsurge in the property market means the government is likely to ask China to let it expand this year's land sales program.
